instruction:
Use the ANSYS Fluent GUI to complete a 2D laminar channel-flow analysis.

Physical problem:
Two-dimensional laminar Poiseuille flow in a straight rectangular channel.

Coordinate system and geometry:
- Use a 2D planar model.
- Use SI units in Fluent.
- The channel length is along the global X direction.
- The channel height is along the global Y direction.
- The channel length is 1000 mm, equivalent to 1.000 m.
- The channel height is 2 mm, equivalent to 0.002 m.
- The computational domain should occupy:
  - 0 ≤ X ≤ 1.000 m
  - 0 ≤ Y ≤ 0.002 m
- The inlet is the boundary at X = 0 m.
- The outlet is the boundary at X = 1.000 m.
- The bottom wall is the boundary at Y = 0 m.
- The top wall is the boundary at Y = 0.002 m.

Boundary zone names:
- Name the inlet boundary: inlet
- Name the outlet boundary: outlet
- Name the bottom wall boundary: bottom
- Name the top wall boundary: top

Model parameters:
- Fluid: water
- Use constant material properties:
  - Density: 998.2 kg/m³
  - Dynamic viscosity: 0.001003 Pa·s
- Mesh:
  - Structured quadrilateral mesh
  - Use sufficient resolution across the channel height to resolve the laminar velocity profile.

Boundary conditions:
- Inlet:
  - Velocity inlet
  - Uniform X-velocity = 0.1 m/s
  - Y-velocity = 0 m/s
- Outlet:
  - Pressure outlet
  - Gauge pressure = 0 Pa
- Top wall:
  - Stationary no-slip wall
- Bottom wall:
  - Stationary no-slip wall

Solver setup:
- Solver type: pressure-based
- Time setting: steady
- Flow model: laminar
- Pressure-velocity coupling: SIMPLE
- Spatial discretization: second-order schemes where applicable
- Initialize the solution and iterate until convergence.

Save requirements:
- Use C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop as the working directory.
- Save the Fluent case file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\poiseuille_2d.cas
- Save the Fluent data file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\poiseuille_2d.dat
